newsitem.title: UK: UK construction output rises one pct in Q1.
newsitem.headline: UK construction output rises one pct in Q1.

text.p: The total volume of UK construction output rose one percent in the first quarter of 1997 from the previous quarter and was four percent higher than in the first quarter of 1996, the Department of Environment said.
It was the fourth consecutive quarterly increase and was mainly due to strong growth in the private commercial, private industrial, public housing repair and maintenance sectors.

Construction minister Nick Raynsford welcomed the figures and said: "The sustained increase in output, combined with a general growth in new orders, shows that the construction industry is slowly moving in the right direction."
The figures are provisional and reflect the volume of construction work (including repair and maintenance) at constant 1990 prices, adjusted to exclude normal seasonal variations.
The total volume of new work in the first quarter was three per cent higher compared with the previous quarter and six per cent higher compared with the same period a year earlier.
The total volume of repair and maintenance work was unchanged from the previous quarter but one per cent higher than in the same 1996 period.
New private housing work in the first quarter of 1997 was two per cent higher compared with the previous quarter and 26 per cent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
New work in the public housing sector in the latest quarter was nine per cent lower than in the previous quarter and eight per cent lower compared with the first quarter of 1996.
New infrastructure output was two per cent higher than in the fourth quarter of 1996 and unchanged compared with the first quarter of 1996.
New construction work in the private industrial sector was eight per cent higher than in the fourth quarter of 1996 and 13 per cent higher compared with the same period a year earlier.
New private commercial output was seven per cent higher compared with the previous quarter and 13 per cent higher than in the first quarter of 1996.
New work in the public non-housing sector (excluding infrastructure) was three per cent lower than in the previous quarter and 16 per cent lower compared with a year earlier.

Housing repair and maintenance work (including improvement work) in the public sector was nine per cent higher compared with the previous quarter but seven per cent lower compared with the same period a year earlier.
Housing repair and maintenance work in the private sector was six per cent lower than in the previous quarter but 13 per cent higher than a year earlier.
Repair and maintenance work in the public non-housing sector in the first quarter was three per cent lower than the previous quarter and 15 per cent lower compared with the first quarter of 1996.
Repair and maintenance work in the private non-housing sector was one per cent higher compared with the previous quarter and eight per cent higher compared than a year earlier.

The seasonally adjusted number of employees in employment in April 1997 was two per cent lower compared with January 1997 but two per cent higher compared with April 1996. Total employment (including the self-employed) in April 1997 was three per cent lower compared with January 1997 but one per cent higher compared with April 1997.
